{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZeGLXA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDFSK4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 41, "title": "Support V30MZ FPO1 and WonderSwan POLL without execution failures", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `9bcbf29727bd4b052991d8937964e25f51ac1a05`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs` rejects POLL/WAIT (`9B`) and FPO1 (`D8`–`DF`) as unsupported opcodes. Software encountering these instructions stops instead of continuing with the documented console behavior. This affects WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal; impact on particular commercial titles remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

Execute FPO1 as a two-byte no-op and POLL as a one-byte, nonblocking console instruction through the ordinary CPU decoder. Preserve architectural state, following-instruction alignment, mapped fetch accounting and existing interrupt/device scheduling.

## Context

The clean checkout and remote main match the baseline. The inspected open Issues/PRs collection is empty; closed history contains no completed equivalent. [Issue #35](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/35) explicitly left FPO1 unresolved. Preserve its BUSLOCK requirements and [Issue #39](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/39) transfer accounting.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), §§1.3/3.6, identifies FPO1 as NOP. Its POLLB description specifies continuation when the input is low; Appendix A supplies execution costs. Its displacement-looking FPO1 table does not alone settle console byte consumption.

The inspected [WSCPUTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md) explicitly describes `D8`–`DF` as two-byte NOPs and `9B` as completing without waiting or exception on WonderSwan. The author calls permanently low POLLB wiring probable, not proven. [Experiment source](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L7909) checks POLL followed by ADC; its FPO1 cases at line 8643 exercise all eight opcodes with second byte `C0`. No physical execution or per-model measurement log was inspected. Wider second-byte coverage below tests the report's stated decode rule without claiming additional physical observations. [Ares decoding](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/blob/c76aaffa6e69778baf9a66d1da04298ac2ed7d1d/ares/component/processor/v30mz/instructions-misc.cpp) corroborates one following-byte consumption but is not hardware proof.

Correction record: the earlier assessment treated FPO1 consumption and console POLL applicability as unresolved prerequisites. Replace that assumption with the reported two-byte FPO1 behavior and nonblocking WonderSwan POLL profile. Record the manual/table discrepancy and experimental limits; do not implement generic x87 operand decoding or claim verified electrical wiring.

Relevant files include CPU/bus tests, `docs/hardware-subset.md`, original fixtures, native integration tests and production browser compatibility scripts. Single-step delivery, other unsupported encodings, full prefetch and absolute CPU timing remain separate gaps.

[Saved #39 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/9bcbf29727bd4b052991d8937964e25f51ac1a05/docs/issue-39-validation.md) reports 116 core tests, 17 integration tests, one adapter test, fixture/build checks and both complete Chromium suites passing. These are Coordinator-reported results; planning inspected source and evidence without rerunning checks.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the source reconciliation and correction above before implementation. Document the effective POLLB-low console profile separately from the author's wiring conjecture. Keep remaining hardware uncertainties explicit.
- [ ] Implement all eight FPO1 opcodes, consuming exactly one following instruction-stream byte regardless of its value. Do not calculate a ModR/M address, consume displacement bytes, access an apparent operand, change registers/flags/memory or raise a coprocessor exception. Implement `9B` without halting, exception or external-device dependency.
- [ ] Fetch every consumed byte through the existing mapped CPU path, including IP and 20-bit wrapping. Use the documented execution components—FPO1 one clock and nonwaiting POLL nine clocks—within the existing additive execution/bus approximation. Record independent execution and fetch expectations separately; do not equate emulator totals with measured physical timing. Advance shared-clock devices once and preserve separate DMA accounting.
- [ ] Add independent literal CPU vectors covering every FPO1 opcode and all 256 following-byte values, POLL, multiple flag/register patterns and a discriminating next instruction. Include memory/displacement-looking bytes and prefix-looking second bytes, sentinels proving no operand access, mapped ROM boundaries, live A0 waits and wrapping. Exercise all three models and applicable mono/color modes. Demonstrate baseline failures before the fix.
- [ ] Cover segment overrides and ineffective BUSLOCK, including seven supported redundant prefixes, without interrupt delivery inside the decoded instruction. Preserve existing REP-on-non-string rejection, unsupported-opcode diagnostics, interrupt shadows, HALT behavior and bounded REP restart behavior. A swallowed second byte must never become a prefix or opcode; an unsupported subsequent instruction must still fail normally.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 cartridge that executes POLL and every FPO1 opcode, records independently expected state/alignment results and fresh completion/boot markers, and succeeds through native and production Chromium/Wasm execution on all three models and restart. Include memory-looking FPO1 bytes and verify actual CPU-written results rather than saved pass markers. Record baseline failure and corrected passes.
- [ ] Preserve existing three-model gates, firmware-free handoff, LCD pipeline, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM and both EEPROM controllers, browser save integrity, input/frame continuity and ROM ownership/provenance. Retain generic unsupported-operation errors; add no blanket NOP fallback or game-specific path.
- [ ] Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against production preview, including the new probe.
- [ ] Update hardware support documentation, fixture provenance and validation evidence. Coordinator reviews the final diff against every acceptance checkbox before merge, records resolved findings and distinguishes tests present from checks actually executed. Preserve unrelated acceptance assertions when correcting obsolete unsupported-instruction expectations.

## Optional validation

Compare the original probe with lawfully available physical-console observations or independent implementations. Additional timing observations may refine documented approximations. Physical hardware, proprietary ROMs/firmware and human gameplay are not prerequisites; no commercial-title compatibility claim follows from this task.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
